explanation: Special folder monitoring -- per-folder honeypot/immutability/activity checks on a set of admin-configured folders, confirmed via a real product QA test spec (2026-08-27). /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_128 reads /athinio/system/param_cmd_128.xml for a list of folders, each with independent flags: honey_pot$idx (place a honeypot copy in that folder and run the same rChecker-style content diff used elsewhere), immutibility$idx (chattr +i any file older than 5 minutes in that folder), and folder_monitor$idx (log a modified/accessed/created activity summary for that folder). It clears athinio/system/secOpsOutput_128 at the start of each run. If ANY configured folder's honeypot check finds ransomware-style corruption (var >= 1 across all folders checked), it logs 'Attack : Ransomeware corruption Found' to secOpsOutput_128 and sets <special_files_honeypot> to 1 in /athinio/system/alertlog.xml, which rolls up directly to Alert.xml's special_files_honeypot tag (confirmed present in Alert.xml's 41-tag schema). If no corruption is found across any configured folder, it logs INFO and sets the flag to 0.

known_patterns.meaning: Drift/tampering detected -- at least one configured special folder's honeypot check found ransomware-style corruption (a content mismatch between a decoy file and its reference copy).

evidence_sources.default_meaning: Clean -- no configured special folder's honeypot copy showed content divergence from its reference. Confirmed live on real hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 (2026-08-27).

metadata.caveat: EVIDENCE QUALITY NOTE (2026-08-27): secOpsOutput_128's top-line verdict ('Attack : Ransomeware corruption Found' / 'INFO : ... Not Found') is a restated conclusion from the same script run that sets special_files_honeypot -- not independent evidence on its own. The genuinely independent, checkable detail is the per-folder scan blocks underneath it (Modified/Accessed/Created timestamps, per file 'Made immutable'/'Failed immutable' lines) -- an LLM verifying this should weigh those blocks, not the top-line verdict, when judging whether the 'not detected' status holds up; if no folders have folder_monitor$idx or immutibility$idx enabled, there may be no such detail to check at all. This is a per-folder-configured feature -- if no folders are configured in param_cmd_128.xml (or none have honey_pot$idx enabled), this check has nothing to actually monitor even though the tag itself will still read 0 (clean by default, not because monitoring ran and found nothing). Distinct from the plain 'honeypot' entry (which watches fixed decoy paths via nerviofsMountPath/Linguard.xml, not admin-configured folders).
